# Narration: gatekeep-pr, PR 642 (re-entry, course `deliver`)

All forge reads and writes below are simulated, as the digest specifies.

## 1. Validate the run record

- The first tracker task names `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. I read that file. It parses, and `consent.target` holds `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`.
- I make no helper dispatch here. I reconcile the in-flight stage `repair.wave.stage: apply` against the stored helper results and the local/remote heads.
  - `/tmp/guard-description.synthetic`: P1's body write was confirmed. Readback matched the exact replacement at unchanged head `1111…1111`. The narrow recheck matched.
  - `/tmp/guard-failed.synthetic`: P2's implementer returned `open`. The scoped test `node --test src/guard.test.ts` printed `not ok 3 - signature comparison is constant-time`. The helper discarded its edits and made no commit.
- I check the worktree directly:
  - `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 status --porcelain` returns empty.
  - `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 rev-parse HEAD` returns `1111…1111`, which equals `pre_wave_head` and `pushed_head`.
- The completed wave is retained for reconciliation. I do not replay it.

## 2. Close out the wave

This follows `fix-wave.md` `## Review before push`.

- HEAD equals `pre_wave_head`, and the only dispatched file payload (P2) returned `open`. So I skip the pre-push reviewer and skip the push.
- The `repair.wave.no_progress` checkpoint is already persisted:
  - failed prerequisite: the scoped test for constant-time comparison
  - observed value: failed
  - result path: `/tmp/guard-failed.synthetic`
- I do not re-dispatch the unchanged payload.
- No round is spent. No commit changed source, so `rounds_used` stays 1. `syncs_used` stays 0, and both caps stay 6.
- P1's affected-claim recheck under `### Description repair` is already complete (matched), so no further recheck runs.
- No push means no loop sync, no CI watch, and no own-push re-render.

## 3. Unchanged head re-enters step 5 through `### Pre-menu refresh`

- `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
  - Head is `1111…1111` (unchanged) and state is OPEN.
  - The body equals the stored replacement body, which is the gate's own write, so it is not a new edit.
  - `baseRefName` is `main`, matching `consent.target`. Mergeable is MERGEABLE and merge state is CLEAN.
- `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
  - Run 910 completed with success.
- No binding check is pending. The Evidence resolution row stays CI-sufficient (`ci / test`).
- No claim-check-only helper is needed, because no claim moved from pending.

## 4. Tracker

- The original init was `gather, provision, verify` (no `--rebase`), and those stages are closed.
- On this re-entry I `add` the `report` stage, and later `menu` when it starts.

## 5. Assessed SHAs

- Verification evidence comes from CI on `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` (run 910, `ci / test` success). No local run happens.
- The brief assesses the same SHA, `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.

## 6. Integrate and run the exit check

- P1 is resolved, so it leaves the rendered list.
- P2 stays open as a blocker.
- Readiness fails because P2 is open.
- The first matching obstacle row is "scoped test unchanged-red after restore". That gives the `### No-progress obstacle`, rendered with the obstacle template.

## 7. Render

No sync line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

```

Blockers:
1. Signature comparison uses ordinary equality instead of a constant-time compare, so response timing can leak how much of a forged signature matches; the repository's review rules require constant-time comparison. (src/guard.ts:18)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

The last repair left an equality fallback and the scoped test still fails, so retrying the same payload cannot pass until the payload or its test input changes. (not ok 3 - signature comparison is constant-time; node --test src/guard.test.ts)

Pick one:
1. deliver - add 6 to the round and sync caps before work and retry; with the failed test and payload unchanged it stops here again.
2. assess - post the open blocker as a review comment on the PR, then stop; no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
```

## Continuation, in order

All operations below are simulated.

1. **Resume the existing run, without initializing another tracker or record.** The invocation has no `--rebase`; its initial tracker stages were `gather`, `provision`, and `verify`. The first task retains `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. I preserve course `deliver`, round usage `1/6`, sync usage `0/6`, and the completed unsuccessful wave.

2. **Validate the record and reconcile the completed attempt.** I run:
   ```sh
   cat /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic
   cat /tmp/guard-description.synthetic
   cat /tmp/guard-failed.synthetic
   cat /tmp/guard-review.synthetic
   ```
   The record matches `meadow/events`, PR `642`, and base `main`. The description write and exact-head narrow recheck already resolved its claim contribution. The file repair returned open, restored its edits, and made no commit. I do not replay either operation.

3. **Confirm the worktree and unchanged source inputs.** I run:
   ```sh
   git -C .worktrees/pr-642 rev-parse --show-toplevel
   git -C .worktrees/pr-642 rev-parse HEAD
   git -C .worktrees/pr-642 status --porcelain
   git -C .worktrees/pr-642 log 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111..HEAD --oneline
   git -C .worktrees/pr-642 show HEAD:src/guard.ts
   git -C .worktrees/pr-642 show HEAD:src/guard.test.ts
   ```
   HEAD remains `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, the tree is clean, and there are no unpushed commits. The failed test's source inputs and the recorded scoped command are unchanged.

4. **Honor the no-progress checkpoint.** The completed attempt remains blocked on `signature comparison is constant-time`. I preserve its failed-prerequisite checkpoint and helper result path. I dispatch **no helper**: another implementer would repeat the unchanged failed attempt, and neither another description recheck nor another reviewer is needed to reconcile the stored results.

   I do not run `node --test src/guard.test.ts`, sync, review before push, push, or watch CI. No round or sync is spent, and no deadline is opened.

5. **Start the report tracker stage and perform the required pre-menu refresh.** I add `report` when it starts, then run:
   ```sh
   gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
   gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
   ```
   The target, head, body, and checks remain unchanged. Verification evidence and the brief's source assessment remain bound to **`1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`**. Existing green CI does not resolve the constant-time comparison defect.

6. **Integrate and select the obstacle template.** The corrected description claim stays resolved. The constant-time comparison finding stays open; I do not invent an independent missing-rejection-test blocker. I complete `report`, add `menu`, and retain the no-progress obstacle.

   No tracker stage is reinitialized, and no helper is dispatched in this continuation. An obstacle delivery selection would add six to each cumulative cap before work, but unchanged prerequisite inputs would immediately exit again without another repair attempt.

## Rendered report and next menu

Delivers: The PR rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. Signature comparison uses ordinary equality instead of the constant-time comparison required by the repository's review rules. Replace it with a constant-time comparison without an equality fallback. (src/guard.ts:18)

The repair attempt failed `signature comparison is constant-time` and restored its edits. Its source inputs and command are unchanged, so delivery cannot retry this attempt. (src/guard.test.ts; signature comparison is constant-time)

No Sync line renders because the invocation did not include `--rebase`.

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - extend each cumulative cap by 6 and retry only after the failed prerequisite changes.
2. assess - post the open blocker as a review comment without repairs.
3. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep P1's confirmed description progress separate from P2's failed file attempt: Before reconciles the wave by stating the P1 write is confirmed via exact readback at the unchanged head and `P1: resolved`, then drops P1 from the rendered list while keeping its ledger ID, and treats P2 alone as the open blocker; After does the same in sections 1, 2 and 6 (P1 readback matched, narrow recheck complete, no further recheck; P2 open; no round spent; P1 leaves the rendered list, P2 stays). Nothing in the After wording moved f3. One small hardening for After: Before explicitly says P1's ID 'stays in the ledger' while leaving the rendered list, whereas After only says P1 'is resolved, so it leaves the rendered list' — adding the ledger-retention clause (and that the saved finding/payload for P1 is not re-opened or rewritten by the no-progress obstacle) would make the independence of description progress from the failed file wave unambiguous under the course model without affecting the deliver/assess/stop menu or cap/round accounting the Change introduces.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved for f3: both outputs keep the confirmed description correction (P1 resolved via the exact-head readback and narrow recheck, not replayed or reopened) separate from the failed P2 file repair (edits restored, no commit, no push, no-progress checkpoint retained). After actually states the independence more explicitly in steps 2 and 6 ("I do not replay either operation", "The corrected description claim stays resolved. The constant-time comparison finding stays open") while delivering the Change's course/cap framing (course deliver, 1/6 and 0/6 usage, obstacle template with deliver/assess/stop). To keep this stable in future wordings, continue to name the two closures separately in the reconciliation step and in the rendered report rather than summarizing the wave as a single failed attempt; one small tightening would be to state in step 1 or 2 that body-only work spent no round, which the Change calls for and After only implies.
